text.p: Comverse Technology Inc said it had completed a $100 million private placement of 5.75 percent convertible subordinated debentures to institutional investors in the United States.
The debentures are convertible into common stock at a conversion price of $45.75 each.

The company said the proceeds would be used for general corporate purposes, including possible acquisitions. Eilon Michaeli, vice president for finance, noted that Comverse already had some $120 million in cash or equivalents prior to the placement but that the company had no immediate plans for what to do with it.

In Nasdaq trading, Comverse's share price fell to $35.60 from $41 after the announcement. Michaeli said this was because some shareholders, particularly hedge funds, sold their Comverse stock after buying the debentures.

Comverse, which has headquarters in Woodbury, New York, but conducts most of its operations in Israel through its Efrat Future Technologies subsidiary, makes and markets computer and telecommunications systems.
